hardware_summary: No on-site generation found at the terminal itself; the terminal is a gas SUPPLIER to two large adjacent merchant gas-fired plants (CNOOC Fujian Gas Power Co., ~1,400 MW / 4x350MW at Xiuyu Port, 'just one street away' and pipeline-interconnected; Xiamen CCGT, 780 MW) rather than the reverse.
captive_summary: Fujian LNG (CNOOC, Putian, operating since 2008) is the province's primary gas supplier and was built to feed regional gas-fired power stations, not to be powered by them. A government economic-development article states the CNOOC Fujian Gas Power plant sits one street from the terminal, pipeline-linked, with 5.2 billion kWh/yr design output (i.e. it draws gas FROM the terminal). A separate developer page confirms Xiamen's 780 MW CCGT plant's feed gas is 'from CNOOC Fujian LNG receiving terminal.' No source describes any on-site/captive generation at the terminal; the direction of the gas-power relationship is outbound (PowerPlantsSupplied), not captive.
confirmed_how: fujian.gov.cn (provincial government portal, coastal-economy feature, 2026): '中海福建燃气发电有限公司燃气电厂与福建LNG接收站仅一街之隔，通过管道互联互通。电厂设计年发电量52亿千瓦时' ('CNOOC Fujian Gas Power's plant is just one street from the Fujian LNG terminal, pipeline-interconnected; the plant's designed annual output is 5.2 billion kWh') — establishes the plant is a separate ~1,400 MW merchant IPP fed BY the terminal. pacificenergycorp.com (developer profile of the Xiamen CCGT plant it built): 'The feed gas is from CNOOC Fujian LNG receiving terminal with LNG from Tangguh, Indonesia' — second independent confirmation of the outbound-supply direction. A CNOOC internal procurement notice (buy.cnooc.com.cn) for '福建LNG内燃机式发电机紧急叫修服务(2023-2026)' (emergency repair service for internal-combustion-engine generators at Fujian LNG) shows the terminal does keep some internal-combustion genset(s) on site, but the notice does not state fuel type, rating, or duty — most likely diesel emergency/safety gensets per standard Chinese LNG-terminal practice, but unconfirmed; flagged in notes rather than counted as a YES per the fuel gate (fuel unstated).

confirms Xiamen CCGT's feed gas sourced from this terminal

gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's prior ('Fujian Sansteel Minguang Co., Ltd. Gas Power Project', tier A, captive=True, 240 MW) is a mismatch. That project is 三钢闽光动力厂's 2x80MW blast-furnace/coal-gas-fired power units at the Sansteel steelworks in Sanming (inland, ~150km from the coastal Putian LNG terminal) — a different fuel (coal/BF gas, not natural gas), a different industrial host (a steel mill's own captive plant), and a different location entirely. It has no relationship to the Fujian LNG terminal. Independent source: https://m.bjx.com.cn/mnews/20231121/1344651.shtml (三钢闽光动力厂煤气发电项目投产发电) describing the Sansteel project.
gogpt_candidate_basis: The GOGPT prior plant is an unrelated steel-mill captive coal-gas plant in a different city; no captive gas generation was found at the Fujian LNG terminal itself. Terminal is grid-connected and is itself a gas SUPPLIER to nearby merchant plants.
notes: PowerPlantsSupplied direction-test case: this terminal supplies feed gas to CNOOC Fujian Gas Power (~1,400 MW merchant IPP, adjacent) and Xiamen CCGT (780 MW) among others — candidate for the PowerPlantsSupplied field in a different (Update) batch, not a captive finding here. Also note a CNOOC procurement contract references on-site internal-combustion generator(s) requiring emergency repair service; fuel type not established from the notice title alone (likely diesel safety/emergency genset per standard practice) — insufficient to change the verdict since fuel is unstated, not confirmed gas.

hardware_summary: No on-site generation; the terminal (PetroChina Kunlun, Fuqing, under construction) is powered entirely by new off-site grid infrastructure: a 220kV line from Huatang substation (38.5km) and a 110kV line from Donghan substation (15.28km), stepped down on-site by two 31.5MVA transformers.
captive_summary: A government project-approval document for the terminal's dedicated 'off-site power supply project' (站外供电工程) describes only external grid-connection works — two new transmission lines from existing regional substations plus two 31.5MVA step-down transformers at the terminal — with no mention anywhere of on-site/backup generation, gas turbines, or gensets. This is a primary/regulatory source and stands alone as green.
confirmed_how: Fuqing municipal government approval notice (fuqing.gov.cn, 2026-03-31) for '福建LNG接收站项目站外供电工程' (off-site power supply project for the Fuqing LNG terminal — this is PetroChina Kunlun's Fuqing-facility project, distinct from CNOOC's older 'Fujian LNG' terminal in Putian despite the similar Chinese name): approves a 220kV line from Huatang substation (38.5km, 36.1km overhead/2.4km cable) and a 110kV line from Donghan substation (15.28km, 14.7km overhead/0.58km cable), with '安装主变2台，容量均为31.5MVA' (two 31.5MVA main transformers) installed at the receiving station; total investment RMB 122.56 million. No on-site generation of any kind is mentioned.
